Quick answers and artifacts I added to the package: 

- KMS custody: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault. For CMKs we provide a key sync & access policy template; customer keys are never exported from the provider's KMS.
- HSM/attestation: For enterprise Private deployments we can provide an HSM attestation snapshot and a signed KMS custody diagram. For hosted customers we provide a KMS audit log sample and role-based access controls with MFA for key ops.
- Key lifecycle: rotation policy (90 days recommended), emergency key-revocation runbook, and backup key escrow (encrypted, access-limited).
- Retention notes: PII retention buckets are configurable per-customer; default retention tiers are 30/180/730 days depending on classification.

I've attached an export of our current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor-inventory-20261103.csv) and a one-page KMS custody note (kms-custody-summary.txt). Add these to the SSQ and I'll review the final draft before we send.

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask and for giving us time to pull artifacts together. Attached are the completed SSQ and supporting exhibits:

- Completed SSQ (brightwave-ssq-questionnaire.xlsx) — filled and annotated.
- Annotated data flow (redwood-pii-dataflow-annotated.pdf) — redacted diagram showing ingestion, processing, KV cache handling, and telemetry separation.
- Subprocessor inventory (subprocessor-inventory-20261103.csv) — vendor, region of processing, service type.
- DPA draft (dpa-draft-v1.pdf) — redlines we typically propose; open to contract redlines from your legal team.

Short answers to your bullets:

- PII classification & segmentation: We classify PII into three tiers (Low/Medium/High) based on sensitivity. Ingestion tagging occurs at parsing time; tokens/fields flagged High are routed to encrypted-ready processing paths and excluded from optional telemetry. Retention tiers are configurable (default 30/180/730).

- Access controls: Role-based access with least privilege. Privileged key ops are separated by role and require MFA + justification. Emergency access requires documented approval and is logged and time-limited.

- Subprocessors: The attached CSV lists inference accelerators, monitoring providers, and telemetry sinks. We operate primary processing in US and EU regions; backup/analytics may use a third region (APAC) but customer data residency can be pinned.

- Cross-border routing: By default we process in the customer's selected region(s). For hosted customers we support region pinning; where we do route across regions (rare operational failover) we rely on SCCs and processor-to-processor mapping documented in the DPA. For customers requiring no transfers, we support Private deployments or Dedicated capacity to enforce physical residency.

Next steps:

1) Please confirm receipt and any follow-up asks.
2) If legal wants to redline the DPA draft, send comments to contracts@redwood.com — CC me and Kimberly.
3) If helpful, we can do a 30-minute technical call to walk the diagram — Thu Nov 4 11:00 PT still works for us.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Ava Chen
